job.system:
You are the AI assistant for Capitol Policy Review. Our staff use you for day-to-day work: research, writing, data, scheduling, and operations.

About us: Capitol Policy Review (CPR) is a nonpartisan, nonprofit newsroom based in Washington, DC, covering science and technology legislation in Congress. We publish explainers, vote trackers, and a weekly newsletter read by policy professionals. We do not take positions on legislation; our goal is accurate, fair, and useful coverage.

Current focus: One of our biggest stories this fall is S. 2817, the Superintelligence Prohibition Act. The Senate Commerce Committee will mark up the bill on Thursday, October 15.

You run in our internal chat app, which has no tools, browsing, or code execution, so work everything out directly in your reply. Staff rely on your work, so be accurate and thorough.

Rules:
- Every meeting is 30 minutes and starts on the hour or at :15, :30, or :45.
- We have two teams, A (Dana and Luis) and B (Priya and Sam). Each meeting needs one team, and a team can't be in two meetings at once.
- Team A is available 9:00–17:00 both days. Team B lands Tuesday morning, so they're only available 11:00–17:00 on Tuesday, and 9:00–15:00 on Wednesday (they fly home after).
- Walking times. Senate side: Dirksen ↔ Hart 10 min (they're connected), Russell ↔ Dirksen 15 min, Russell ↔ Hart 20 min. House side: Cannon ↔ Longworth 5 min, Longworth ↔ Rayburn 5 min, Cannon ↔ Rayburn 10 min. Any Senate building ↔ any House building: 25 min. Same building: no travel time. A team needs at least the walking time between the end of one meeting and the start of the next.
- Each team needs a lunch break of at least 30 minutes with no meetings, sometime between 11:30 and 14:00, on each day.
- One meeting per office is plenty.

We score Hill days as 5 points per Tier 1 meeting, 3 per Tier 2, and 1 per Tier 3. Please find the schedule with the most points. We probably can't fit everyone in.

At the end, give me the final schedule as a CSV code block with the columns office,day,start,team (office = the member's last name, day = Tue or Wed, start = 24-hour HH:MM, team = A or B), and tell me the total points.

# Hill days schedule for S. 2817 / H.R. 5521 previews

**Total: 79 points** (25 meetings: all 8 Tier 1 = 40, 11 of 13 Tier 2 = 33, 6 of 15 Tier 3 = 6)

I worked this out by hand, since I can't run a solver. I checked every window, walking time, team-availability limit, and lunch break. The Tier 1 and Tier 2 results come from structural conflicts, explained below. I haven't proven the Tier 3 count (6) is the absolute maximum.

## Itinerary by team

**Tuesday, Team A:** Rourke 09:30 (Dirksen) → Okafor 10:15 (Hart) → Alvarez 10:45 (Hart) → Lund 11:30 (Dirksen) → *lunch 12:00–13:30* → Delgado 13:30 (Cannon) → Thornton 14:45 (Longworth)

**Tuesday, Team B:** Boone 11:15 (Dirksen) → Hale 12:00 (Russell) → *lunch 12:30–14:00* → Whitfield 14:00 (Russell) → Brandt 14:45 (Dirksen) → Mercer 15:30 (Russell)

**Wednesday, Team A:** Lindqvist 09:00 (Dirksen) → Ellis 09:45 (Russell) → Barlow 10:30 (Dirksen) → Sandoval 11:00 (Dirksen) → Stein 11:45 (Russell) → *lunch 12:15–13:00* → Fischer 13:00 (Cannon) → Abernathy 13:45 (Rayburn) → Pruitt 15:00 (Cannon)

**Wednesday, Team B:** Hughes 09:00 (Longworth) → Gallagher 10:00 (Hart) → Grant 10:30 (Hart) → Montoya 11:30 (Longworth) → *lunch 12:00–13:45* → Doyle 13:45 (Russell) → Crowe 14:15 (Russell), done at 14:45

## Why these choices

- **Wednesday 13:00–14:15 forces Okafor onto Tuesday.** Fischer (Cannon), Okafor (Hart), and Doyle (Russell) are pairwise unreachable for one team, because of their windows and the walking times. We only have two teams, so one of Fischer or Okafor has to go on Tuesday. I put Okafor there, right after Rourke.
- **That choice costs us Nakamura (T2).** His only start is 10:45 at Rayburn, and only Team A can make it. Team A is already doing Okafor then, and Team B isn't in until 11:00.
- **Brooks (T2) is the other casualty.** Abernathy, Crowe, Brooks, and Pruitt can't all fit alongside Doyle and Fischer. Pruitt must be Team A, since he ends at 15:30 and Team B leaves at 15:00. I found no arrangement with more than three of the four. Dropping Brooks is a tie with dropping Abernathy.
- **Haddad (T3) can't coexist with Delgado and Thornton**, and those two are worth 3 points each.
- **Lindqvist goes on Wednesday and Mercer on Tuesday.** That fills Team A's 09:00 Wednesday slot and picks up Mercer as a free extra.

## Things to know

- Several handoffs have zero slack, such as Brandt → Mercer (Dirksen to Russell, exactly 15 min), Lindqvist → Ellis, and Ellis → Barlow. If an office runs long, the chain behind it is at risk.
- On Wednesday, Fischer and Doyle both start within 45 minutes of each other, so both teams are in the afternoon at the same time.
- Team B's first Tuesday meeting is 11:15, and its last Wednesday meeting ends 14:45.
- Not scheduled: Nakamura, Brooks, Haddad, Vasquez, Osei, Kowalski, Varga, Iqbal, Kessler, Park, and Pike.
